messages.content:
You are FIXING a short WhatsApp quiz written for the children who sat in ONE real lesson. 1 of its 8 questions were rejected by our checks. You are writing ONE replacement for each. Every other question is good and is staying exactly as it is — do not touch it, do not return it.

QUIZ LANGUAGE: English. Write EVERYTHING in English — every stem, option, explanation and feedback — even though the lesson was taught in Urdu: translate the teacher's own words and keep the lesson's own examples, numbers and names. An Urdu word may appear only when quoting a term the class used, in quotation marks.

REWRITE THESE QUESTIONS: q6

WHAT THESE CHILDREN WERE MEANT TO LEARN. A replacement stays on its own question's SLO, at its own question's level.
- S1 [taught at understand] Recognise the place value of each digit in 2-digit numbers (tens, ones/units).
- S2 [taught at understand] Count objects and numbers to and across 99 (2-digit numbers) forwards and backwards, beginning from zero one, or from any given number.
- S3 [taught at understand] Read a 2-digit number from a tens-and-ones picture: tens circles first, then loose counters.
- S4 [taught at recall] Identify that one circle of 10 counters means one ten, and a loose counter means one one.
- S5 [taught at understand] Write the tens digit first, then the ones digit, for a 2-digit number.

THE LESSON'S OWN MATERIAL — dress the replacement in it, so a child recognises the class in the quiz.
topic as the teacher named it: Guess the number from base-ten pictures
the lesson's own examples: A picture showing 6 tens circles and 1 loose counter, representing the number 61.; Counting 6 tens as 60 and 1 one as 1, leading to 60 + 1 = 61.; The number 62 as the next number after 61 on a number strip.; A picture representing 24, which children might misinterpret as 6 marks.; Stepping forward twice from 68 on a number strip.; Stepping back once from 70 on a number strip.; 5 tens and 6 ones is 50 and 6, which is 56.
the words used in class: place value, 2-digit numbers, tens, ones, units, counters

THE QUESTIONS THAT ARE STAYING. A replacement must not ask one of these again, and must not have the same answer as one of them.
  q0: What does one loose counter mean?
  q1: What number do these show?
  q2: In the number 61, what is the value of the digit '6'?
  q3: What number is 2 steps forward from 68?
  q4: How do you write 5 tens and 6 ones?
  q5: What number is 1 step back from 70?
  q7: Which of these are 'tens' and 'ones'?

EVERY QUESTION TESTS SOMETHING NO OTHER QUESTION TESTS. No two questions in the quiz may have the same correct answer on the same fact: the same question with its options in another order, with other wrong options, or with a few words added or changed is the SAME question, and a child would answer it twice. A question shape may be used again only with different numbers or a different item from the lesson (round 18, then round 16; the article before "kite", then before "tree"), so that its correct answer is different too. Before you return, read the questions side by side: where two test the same thing, write a question on something else in place of the later one, keeping the number of questions as it is.

REJECTED — write one new question for each, except a question marked REPAIR IN PLACE: return that one as it stands, with only the words its complaints name changed.

q6 · slo_id "S3" · level "understand"
  the question being thrown away: "What number does the picture show?"
  its options were: 61 | 16 | 7
  why it was rejected:
    - q6: FIGURE_NUMBERS — the stem uses 60 but the picture's spec does not carry it; draw every number the question needs

A RE-WORDING OF A REJECTED QUESTION IS REJECTED AGAIN (except a question rejected ONLY for length, ONLY for how it speaks to the child, ONLY for two English terms side by side, ONLY for a name in English letters, or ONLY for the language of its teacher notes — see LENGTH, THE CHILD HAS NO GENDER, TWO ENGLISH TERMS SIDE BY SIDE, A NA…(+12393)
